claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a native heterogeneous oxide film.
Q235 steel contains inherent Mn-rich inclusions.
Q235 steel contains inherent Si-rich inclusions.
The heterogeneous native oxide and Mn- and Si-rich inclusions form localized galvanic cells.
These localized galvanic cells promote the early onset of pitting corrosion in chloride-rich environments.
Elevated temperature promotes the proposed localized corrosion process.
Mechanical polishing followed by electrochemical passivation can produce a more uniform oxide layer on Q235 steel.
The proposed surface treatment can alter only oxide characteristics while leaving the underlying microstructure unmodified.
Oxide-film quality and inclusion-induced local electrochemical potential differences establish galvanic cells at the oxide/matrix interface.
The heterogeneous oxide creates localized differential-aeration regions.
Under chloride attack and thermal stress, differential aeration and galvanic coupling catalyze pitting corrosion.
A uniformly passivated oxide layer minimizes localized galvanic effects and suppresses corrosion initiation.
Passivated specimens will have lower pit density than untreated specimens.
Passivated specimens will exhibit more homogeneous corrosion morphology than untreated specimens.
Passivated specimens will exhibit higher EIS impedance than untreated specimens.
Passivated specimens will exhibit lower corrosion-current density than untreated specimens.
The corrosion differences between passivated and untreated specimens will be more pronounced at 60°C than at 25°C.
The proposed findings may not extrapolate from controlled salt-spray exposure to environments with different chemical or mechanical stressors.

contradictions.description: The design defines the untreated oxide as heterogeneous and the treated oxide as uniform, but the falsification rule requires surface analysis to show uniform oxide characteristics without a significant difference between treatments. That condition indicates failure to establish the intended oxide contrast rather than a valid mechanistic falsification.
